chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Jamilyah from Humran from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who made a bequest at the time of his death saying: 'Free so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so.' I looked at his one-third share, but the wealth did not reach the value of the five slaves whom he ordered to be freed. He said: 'Look at those he named and began with freeing them; they are appraised. Look at his one-third share, and he frees from it the first one, then the second, then the third, then the fourth, then the fifth. If the one-third share is insufficient, it falls upon the one he named last, because he freed after the reach of the one-third share what he did not possess, so that is not permissible for him.'
ai.seo_question: How is the estate distributed when a person bequeaths freeing more slaves than the one-third share can cover?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that when the cost of freeing all named slaves exceeds one-third of the estate, the bequest is executed sequentially from the one-third share, with the final named slave bearing the burden of the excess from the owner's remaining two-thirds. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the testator's explicit order of naming takes precedence in determining priority, ensuring the validity of the bequest while respecting the fixed limit of the one-third share for non-heirs.
